The meal that comes second in the day, after breakfast, is lunch.

Regarding the thematic structure of the text, the author’s motive appears to be illustrating the parallel between botanical decay and human emotional isolation. By linking the wilting of the sunflower to the protagonist’s sadness and battles with isolation, the author uses the natural cycle of life and decay as a metaphor to explore themes of human connection. The motive is to urge readers to reflect on how neglect affects both plants and personal relationships, thereby highlighting the importance of care and connection in preventing emotional withering.
